title: Introduce staged prompt-change sweeper with cost-aware smoke replayer
author: Asha Menon
description: Context: Our CI runs full prompt-set smoke evals on every eval-harness change which has led to unpredictable CI token cost and long cycles. This PR introduces a staged "prompt-change sweeper" and a targeted smoke replayer that: computes deterministic, normalization-aware fingerprints for prompt sets, diffs incoming prompt-set changes at cohort granularity, and triggers only the minimal set of smoke evaluations for impacted cohorts. It also adds a configurable cost-aware gate so CI budgets are respected during large rollouts. Motivation: reduce CI token spend and speed up feedback for prompt-set and evaluation-code changes while preserving regression signal for production cohorts. Design summary: 1) Fingerprinting: deterministic normalization pipeline (unicode normalization, whitespace folding, canonicalization of placeholders, and optional semantic-hash via sentence-transformer L2 hash) to produce stable 64-bit fingerprints per prompt and cohort-level aggregate signatures. 2) Sweeper: CLI + staged worker that compares fingerprints from HEAD vs base and emits a minimal delta manifest (affected cohorts + change type: add/modify/remove). 3) Targeted replayer: smoke replayer consumes delta manifest and re-runs only affected prompt subsets with preserved randomness seeds and fixed eval fixtures to produce comparable regression metrics. 4) Cost gate: CI step reads token-estimate for requested replays and blocks if budget threshold exceeded; optional auto-shrinker reduces sample size to fit budget with prioritized cohorts. 5) Reporting: compact regression summary (semantic diffs, token delta estimates, SLO deltas) uploaded to PR comment and to Linear. Implementation highlights: - New module eval_harness/fingerprint.py implements normalization and a purely-deterministic tokenization wrapper; uses cached token maps to ensure stable IDs across runs. - New eval_harness/sweeper.py implements a two-phase compare (fast signature check then per-prompt diff for candidates). - New eval_harness/replayer.py implements the targeted smoke runner and integrates with existing eval runners. - CI: .github/workflows/eval-ci.yml gains a new job "delta-smoke" which runs the sweeper, estimates cost, and conditionally triggers the replayer via workflow_dispatch to limit concurrent token consumption. - Add cost gate config at ci/cost_gate.yaml with sensible defaults and project overrides. - Tests: unit tests for fingerprint normalization and integration smoke test that replays a 10-prompt cohort locally. Usage: CLI: "python -m eval_harness.sweeper --base main --head HEAD --out delta.json" and the CI will pick delta.json to drive the replayer. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on ci flags for two weeks, initial sampling on low-risk cohorts, monitor regression scores and CI token burn. Backout: revert workflow change or disable delta-smoke flag. Testing & validation: local unit tests, integration replay against synthetic cohorts, staged rollout in CI with sample-size throttling. Related: ties to ENG-4521 (eval cost reduction initiative) and SUP-1987 (support ticket showing a costly regression run).

review_comments: Miguel Ortiz: Overall strong idea and the deterministic fingerprinting is necessary. Two concerns: 1) canonicalization might hide intentional whitespace differences used by some prompt tests, 2) we need an audit trail for the exact normalizer used for each run. Please add a normalizer version string to the manifest.

Asha Menon: Added normalizer_version to delta manifest and documented the exact normalization pipeline in docs/eval/delta-sweeper.md. Kept an option to opt-out of semantic-hash stage for deterministic-only runs.
Priya Kapoor: Please ensure the replayer keeps per-prompt seeds stable and records RNG source. Also add a smaller default sample for CI to fit token budgets.
Asha Menon: Replayer now persists rng_seed in replay metadata and cost_gate supports automatic shrink-to-budget. Added unit tests for seed stability.
Samir Patel: CI job looked flaky on first run due to a network timeout on model fetch. Can we retry or vendor a small test model?
Asha Menon: Added retry logic for model fetch and fallback to a lightweight local fixture for the CI dry-run path. Reran CI and green after re-run.
ci_checks: e2e eval (CI delta-smoke): initial run failed due to fetch timeout, re-run passed
notes_on_review: Addressed reviewer feedback: added normalizer_version to ensure auditability, persisted rng_seed, added retry/fallback for CI model fetch, and implemented cost-based auto-shrink. Miguel and Priya approved after follow-ups; Samir approved after CI stabilizations.
release_notes: Add delta-driven prompt-change sweeper and targeted smoke replayer to dramatically reduce CI token usage and speed up regression feedback loops. Opt-in via CI flag; includes cost gate to respect token budgets and an audit trail for normalization. See docs/eval/delta-sweeper.md for usage.
post_merge_actions: Monitor CI token burn for two weeks under ENG-4521 dashboard, enable auto-shrink on repositories exceeding budget thresholds, follow-up to instrument downstream metrics in Redwood Console per-route token deltas.
testing_summary: Unit coverage added for normalize_prompt edge cases; integration test replays a synthetic cohort and validates identical metric outputs when no drift is present. CI delta-smoke tested in feature-flagged mode on a canary repo before org-wide rollout.
